_about: Frozen configuration for `qhld eval fidelity`. Unlike the labelled query set
beside it, this asset carries no judgements: brute-force search is the ground
truth, so nothing here needs adjudicating and the sample can be any size.
The sample itself is NOT stored. The corpus is re-extracted regularly, so a
stored id list would rot silently or force a migration on every re-extraction.
The seed plus a hash of the drawn ids identifies it instead: a re-run either
reproduces the fingerprint or it does not, and the report says which. Same
reasoning as the eval-XV-1 corpus dump, where the artifact of record is the
hash rather than the file.
Recorded per collection at the corpus state the baseline was measured on.
A mismatch does not invalidate a run — it means the numbers are not
comparable to that baseline, which is exactly what needs saying out loud.
Recorded 2026-08-15 at 32,871 / 31,407 points respectively.

filters.label: lang=es
filters.note: ~88% of the collection: the widest filter real traffic produces.

filters.label: group=GP+2025
filters.note: Two conditions, and near the full_scan_threshold=10000KB boundary (~2500 points at 1024 float32 dims) where Qdrant switches between graph traversal and an exhaustive scan of the filtered subset.

filters.label: constituency=Malaga
filters.note: Under 2% — the regime where a restrictive filter is most likely to disconnect the graph, which is the whole reason payload_m and full_scan_threshold exist.

_about: Default arms. `exact` is never listed: it is the ground truth every cell is
scored against, recomputed per filter and per collection.
The uncompressed collection isolates the graph from quantization: measured
against it, HNSW's own error is the only thing left. It is deliberately kept
at a pre-Phase-3 corpus state (31,407 points vs the serving collection's
32,871) — graph navigability at 31K and at 33K points is the same question,
and re-indexing it would cost a full re-embed for no change in the answer.
